questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous by encouraging them to follow you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Reduce throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the most important thing is to see the road behind and to the side of you.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow for movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
Use a lot of throttle to help you get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it does not become loose and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: When riding over a rough surface, grip the handlebars firmly. This helps you keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: What percentage of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake supply?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should a face shield do?

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides.
Prevent air from passing through it.
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting underneath it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, hard to penetrate, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and leave room for glasses if needed.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Know the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle sits lower with a passenger's extra weight. Ride a bit more slowly than usual, especially through curves and corners. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, or stop, so keep a larger space cushion.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rear brake on slippery surfaces, such as wet pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Is braking in a turn easier or more difficult than braking on a straightaway?

options.text: Easier than braking on a straightaway.
More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
Done safely by using the front brake only.
Done safely by using the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the system.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you should tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Start the engine first. Then have the passenger get on. They should sit as far forward as comfortable, hold your waist or belt firmly, and keep both feet on the footrests at all times.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when it is warm outside?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove it and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Many jackets are made to keep riders cool even on warm days.

questions.question: What should you do to increase your visibility?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright, reflective clothing and change your lane position as needed to stay visible to other drivers.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making mirrors hard to use.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering dangerous. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely get off the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, the best way to stop is to:

options.text: Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and slow down by releasing the throttle. Gradually apply the brake of the working tire. Edge toward the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: For protection, motorcycle pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some leg.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snugly without flapping but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Which of these is not protective eyewear for riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Contact lenses
questions.explanation: You must wear protective eyewear such as glasses, goggles, or a face shield. Contact lenses do not meet this requirement.

questions.question: Riding alongside another motorcyclist:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Lets you communicate with the other rider.
Makes it easier for other cars to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. Riding side-by-side limits both riders' escape options if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In dangerous areas like intersections, shopping centers, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: What is true about a windshield?

options.text: It works as well as a face shield.
It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
It is required on all motorcycles.
You should use it only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not give the same protection as goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together to see better.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power can the front brake provide?
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which body part operates the gearshift lever?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other rules signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes a person legally intoxicated?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while drunk.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Planning to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of turn signals. When the left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes left.

questions.question: Which colors make riders most visible?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be seen by other drivers.
